subject: Runway request: Elysian production commit — token pressure, headroom and GPU slab ask
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@elysian.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@elysian.ai
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production commit timing and capacity ask for Elysian pilot

Hi Markus / Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Elysian ops team is excited to move from pilot to a small production commit (targeting 100k monthly active users in Q2). Procurement asked us to get a clear ask for dedicated capacity (GPU slabs) and an SLO fit assessment before the contract signature.

High level workload: Our inference profile is an NLU-heavy 2-turn chat (avg prompt ~420 tokens, avg response ~780 tokens). Traffic profile for the first 90 days is expected to be spiky: morning and evening peaks (approx 65% of daily load in those windows). We estimate 2.5M tokens/day initially, with bursts up to ~450 tokens/sec observed in our internal load tests.

Can you provide a recommended dedicated slab sizing (GPUs / baseline TPS), expected p95 latency for the chosen model family, and suggested headroom for bursts? Also, we need a canary plan and an estimated monthly cost for the reserved slab.

Attaching the token profile CSV the team shared. Let us know if you need more telemetry.

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Head of Ops, Elysian AI

Attachment: elysian_token_profile.csv (CSV, 26 KB)

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Rao <asha@elysian.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production commit timing and capacity ask for Elysian pilot

Asha — thanks for the profile, this is helpful. Looping Karthik & Lauren from capacity/modeling and Ben for ops playbook.

Quick summary of what we'll deliver in the next 48 hours:
- Ballpark slab recommendation (GPU count + model variant) to meet the target burst and steady-state
- SLO mapping (token/s, p95 latency estimates) and a recommended safety headroom percentage
- Canary run plan and roll-forward/fallback model options
- Cost estimate for a 3-month reserved slab (monthly commit + expected overage behavior)

Notes / quick reads: based on the avg token lengths you sent, early intuition is that the workload is response-heavy — KV cache and prefix caching will help on repeat prompts, but initial warm-up on the first query per session will dominate. If you can confirm session length distribution (how many distinct sessions per day vs repeated interactions), that will materially change headroom math.

I'm attaching a sizing workbook with an initial run (columns: token_profile, per-request tokens, modeled TPS, p95 estimate). Karthik — can you push the model run with the 13B quantized v2 (q4) and the 7B_opt baseline and drop numbers in the sheet? Aim to include measure of tail sensitivity to 20% burst uplift.

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: elysian_sizing_model_v1.xlsx (Excel, 180 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Asha Rao <asha@elysian.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 14:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production commit timing and capacity ask for Elysian pilot

Markus / team / Asha — I ran the sizing sweeps and summarized the findings below. I included the workbook tabs: steady_state, burst_20pct, model_comparison. See attached sim outputs and a short notes file (canary_run_notes.txt).

Executive summary (numbers are our modeled medians with conservative buffers):
- Baseline models tested: 13B_q4 (recommended default), 7B_opt (fallback cheaper), 70B_fp16 (not recommended for cost).
- Expected steady-state token/sec (aggregate): 200 tps (matches your 2.5M tokens/day across lower-traffic windows).
- Observed burst 95th percentile (modeled): 420 tps during peak windows; 99th sim captures up to 520 tps for short spikes.
- For the 13B_q4: median p95 generation latency per request at 420 tps aggregate is ~210 ms per token (end-to-end median response p95 ~820 ms).
- For the 7B_opt: p95 generation latency at same load is ~145 ms per token (end-to-end ~560 ms) but with lower quality for some entity resolution prompts — needs prompt-specific eval.

Recommended slab sizing and headroom:
- Conservative committed slab: 4 x A10-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) configured with 13B_q4. This gives sustainable aggregate serving up to ~450 tps with ~20% headroom for short bursts and expected p95 end-to-end ~900 ms under burst.
- Burst allowance / autoscale: allow 2 ephemeral GPUs (burst pool) for constrained peak windows above committed slab for short durations. Fallback policy: if burst capacity unavailable, route to 7B_opt variant with lower latency but slightly lower quality.
- Canary and rollout plan: 72-hour canary with 10% of traffic routed to the dedicated slab, synthetic load generator simulating your morning/evening peaks; evaluate prompt-level regression on entity resolution prompts. If quality regressions exceed 1.5% false positive delta, pause rollout and run rollback.

Cost estimate (rough, list price bucket):
- Reserved 4x A10 slab (monthly commit): $42,000/month (region discounts may apply).
- Estimated additional ephemeral usage (10% overage): ~$4,500/month.
- Implementation / on-boarding one-time: $6,000 (SRE/ops support + canary runs).

Attachments: elysian_sizing_model_v1.xlsx (detailed sims), canary_run_notes.txt.

Notes on sensitivity: SLO headroom is sensitive to session churn. If distinct sessions exceed our baseline (lots of cold KL cache misses), effective per-token latency rises ~25-40% and you should consider +1 GPU reserved. Also, quantization variance on some few-shot prompts can increase latency unpredictably; we'll flag exact prompt families during the canary.

Next steps: Markus to confirm recommended ask to procurement and provide formal proposed commit. Asha — does procurement need a formal SKU/contract line item or is a simple monthly commit figure OK to proceed?

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Capacity Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: canary_run_notes.txt (TXT, 2 KB); elysian_sizing_model_v1.xlsx (Excel, 180 KB)

From: Asha Rao <asha@elysian.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procurement@elysian.ai, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production commit timing and capacity ask for Elysian pilot

Thanks Markus / Karthik — this is exactly what procurement needed. The summary is clear and gives us a path forward.

Procurement request: please convert the conservative committed slab and burst allowance into a contract line with a SKU and monthly committed amount. We will aim to sign a 6-month reserved commitment pending legal review; procurement will follow up with the PO process by next week.

Operational asks before canary: 1) a short runbook for the fallback routing to 7B_opt (who will own runbooks at Redwood ops), 2) the canary load generator script or a hosted link so our SREs can reproduce locally, and 3) a quick checklist for post-canary quality gating (metrics and thresholds).

We will start onboarding infra this month — can you target the canary for the week of Mar 21?

Appreciate the speed.

—
Asha Rao
Head of Ops, Elysian AI
